message.content:
Proteins that reside in the plasma membrane can be grouped into several functional families. Below is a quick reference of the most common types, along with a few representative examples for each category: | Functional class | Typical role | Representative proteins (human) | |-------------------|--------------|----------------------------------| | **Integral membrane receptors** | Bind extracellular signals and trigger intracellular pathways |
  • G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs): β‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin
  • Receptor tyrosine kinases: EGFR, HER2/neu
  • Ion‑channel receptors: NMDA receptor, nicotinic acetylcholine receptor
| | **Ion channels** | Conduct specific ions across the membrane |
  • Voltage‑gated Na⁺ channel (Nav1.5)
  • Voltage‑gated K⁺ channel (Kv1.2)
  • Calcium‑activated chloride channel (TMEM16A)
| | **Transporters / carriers** | Move solutes (sugars, amino acids, ions) via facilitated diffusion or active transport |
  • Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)
  • Sodium‑glucose cotransporter 1 (SGLT1)
  • Chloride channel protein 1 (CLCN1)
| | **Adhesion molecules** | Mediate cell–cell or cell–extracellular matrix interactions |
  • Cytoskeletal linkers: integrins (α5β1)
  • Cadherins: E‑cadherin (CDH1)
  • Selectins: L‑selectin (SELL)
| | **Enzymes** | Catalyze reactions at the membrane surface |
  • Alkaline phosphatase (ALPL)
  • Phosphatidylinositol 3‑kinase (PI3K)
  • Protein kinase C (PKC) isoforms anchored to the membrane
| | **Peripheral / lipid‑anchored proteins** | Associate loosely with the membrane or are tethered via lipid modifications |
  • GPI‑anchored proteins: CD59, CD55
  • Peripheral membrane proteins: actin‑binding proteins (e.g., ezrin)
| | **Signal transduction adaptors** | Scaffold signaling complexes |
  • Grb2
  • Shc
  • LAT (linker for activation of T cells)
| ### How to explore more If you’re interested in a comprehensive, curated list for a specific cell type or organism, you can query a database such as UniProt or the Human Protein Atlas. For example, the **Human Protein Atlas** provides sub‑cellular localization data for thousands of proteins, including those annotated as “plasma membrane.” Feel free to let me know if you’d like a deeper dive into any particular category, or if you have a specific organism or cell type in mind!
